facts.fact: President Chapo promulgated the National Payments System Law by decree, reported by Lusa on 2026-06-13 as 'signed into force'; the Presidency says it updates the legal framework governing the payments system (no promulgation date given, so the published date is used).

Parliament approved in principle, by consensus of all four benches, the proposed national payments system law on the Tuesday before 2026-04-15, to adjust the Bank of Mozambique's powers, improve sanctions and cover secured transactions and insolvency (reported by Lusa).

facts.fact: The Council of Ministers approved the proposal for the new National Payments System (SNP) Law and will submit it to parliament, possibly in the session opening 2026-02-25, per spokesperson Inocencio Impissa (document dated 2026-02-18; no session date given).

At the start of 2026 Mozambique had three electronic money institutions authorised by the central bank, M-Pesa, e-Mola and M-Kesh, owned by the three mobile operators; the document names no law or rule they are licensed under.

facts.fact: Banco de Moçambique announces that Law No. 15/2026 of 2 July approves the National Payment System Law and repeals Law No. 2/2008 of 27 February; the notice gives no start date, so as_of is the law's date of 2 July 2026.

facts.fact: Aviso n.º 1/GBM/2026 of 25 February 2026 is issued by the Banco de Moçambique under Lei n.º 2/2008 of 27 February, the Lei do Sistema Nacional de Pagamentos, which the notice treats as the enabling payments law at that date.

facts.fact: Article 8 of the Regulation annexed to Aviso n.º 1/GBM/2026 makes participation in the Mozambique Instant Payment System (SPIM) compulsory for electronic money institutions and for credit institutions with 5,000 active accounts or 10,000 transfers a year; Article 7 also requires participants to be connected to the national electronic payments network; in force 2 March 2026.
